note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Sparse attention loses recall; MATCH adds an external retriever whose retrieved positions are unmasked, with evidence from benchmarks and ablations

nodes.name: Full attention is quadratic
nodes.description: Full softmax attention costs O(N^2) in computation and memory, limiting practical context length.

nodes.name: Sparse attention hurts recall
nodes.description: Sparse and linear attention (sliding window, Mamba) cut cost but have local windows or fixed-size states that constrain retrieval across distant positions, degrading tasks needing precise long-range recall.

nodes.name: Sparse patterns are context-dependent
nodes.description: Sparse attention patterns in LLMs are highly context-dependent, so selectively retrieving relevant information needs dynamic, context-adaptive attention.

nodes.name: MATCH retrieval module
nodes.description: MATCH splits the context into fixed-size chunks (length U), retrieves top-K chunks by bi-encoder (Sentence-BERT) dot product, reranks them with a cross-encoder, and keeps the top-k (K > k) to balance speed and precision.

nodes.name: Retrieved positions unmasked in attention
nodes.description: MATCH unmasks retrieved token positions in the attention mask (alongside causal and sliding-window masks), so the sparse-attention KV cache stays constant-size and retrieved positions are fixed regardless of sequence length, making memory constant with context length.

nodes.name: KV recomputation in decoding
nodes.description: During decoding, retrieved raw inputs are fed as auxiliary inputs and their KVs recomputed at each layer once per decoding chunk, then cached in a fixed-size temporary cache for reuse.

nodes.name: MQAR near-perfect
nodes.description: On MQAR, MATCH matches full attention and, at sequence length 512, stays near-perfect while other sparse baselines (StreamingLLM, Strided, Random) degrade toward random guessing.

nodes.name: MAD gains
nodes.description: On MAD in-context retrieval tasks, MATCH raises average performance for Hymba from 64.0 to 92.4 (U=2) and for SWA from 59.9 to 89.4, a 45-50% boost.

nodes.name: LongBench gains
nodes.description: On LongBench, MATCH consistently improves overall average across sparsity levels and models, with up to +15.1 on synthetic tasks, and is mostly on par with or better than RAG using the same retrieved content.

nodes.name: NIAH gains
nodes.description: On Needle-in-a-Haystack (8K-128K), MATCH outperforms the sparsified baselines Qwen3 and Phi-3 at all context lengths, especially at 32K-128K.

nodes.name: Random retrieval fails
nodes.description: Replacing the retriever with random indices (Qwen3, 80% SWA, k=8) underperforms both MATCH (34.1 vs 37.0 avg) and the sparse baseline, so gains come from relevant retrieved context, not extra KV pairs.

nodes.name: Beats KV-cache compression baselines
nodes.description: With 50%-sparsified Qwen3 and k=8, MATCH reaches the highest LongBench average (43.4), beating StreamingLLM and FlexPrefill, with the lowest TTFT and decoding memory at 32K.

nodes.name: Efficiency at 90K tokens
nodes.description: At 90K tokens MATCH has TTFT of 4.98s (68% below full attention's 15.88s, close to SWA's 4.62s) and 32% less memory than full attention (18.72 vs 27.67 GiB).

isolated_nodes.name: k=4 matches k=8
isolated_nodes.description: On LongBench, MATCH with k=4 performs about as well as with k=8.

isolated_nodes.name: Chunked prefill
isolated_nodes.description: MATCH uses chunk-wise pre-filling with a retrieval mask, and continual training adapts model parameters to attend to positions outside the sliding window.

isolated_nodes.name: KV compression is complementary
isolated_nodes.description: KV cache compression addresses post-hoc memory storage, whereas MATCH enhances sparse attention for in-context retrieval; the two approaches are complementary.

structural_reasoning: Problem (quadratic cost, sparse-attention recall loss) leads to the retrieval-augmented sparse attention design, then to empirical results, ablation and efficiency analysis.
